Meta and funds managed by Blue Owl Capital formed a joint venture (Blue Owl 80%, Meta 20%) to develop and own Hyperion; ~$27B total development cost; Meta leases the facilities with a 16-year residual value guarantee; >2 GW of compute when complete.

LED: Meta selects 2,250-acre Franklin Farm megasite for $10B, 4 million sq ft AI data center; 500+ direct jobs; 5,000 construction workers at peak; Meta to bring at least 1,500 MW of new renewable energy and restore more water than it consumes.
Entergy Louisiana: 'Claims that critical information is being withheld are simply false' (spokesperson Brandon Scardigli), responding to intervenors in the 7-plant case.

Meta President Dina Powell McCormick at the All-In Summit: the teacher bonuses were 'not our idea'; a parish law sends extra sales tax to school staff pay. Also: 'if a community doesn't want one of our data centers, they get to choose.' The parish superintendent said sales tax collections peaked about 260% above normal during construction.

opposition.what: Earthjustice filed a motion for the Alliance for Affordable Energy and Union of Concerned Scientists asking regulators to require Meta and its developer Laidley LLC to share project information (energy demand, expedited timeline, local jobs) or dismiss Entergy's 3-plant application (docket U-37425).

Follow-up to the March 2025 motion: administrative law judge Melanie Verzwyvelt ruled that Meta and Laidley LLC do not have to join Entergy's case (docket U-37425) as parties, siding with Entergy. Outcome: motion denied; groups said they would seek depositions instead.

Outcome of docket U-37425: the LPSC approved Entergy's three gas plants for the original Hyperion campus 4-1 on 2025-08-20, over objections from the Alliance for Affordable Energy and Union of Concerned Scientists; Commissioner Davante Lewis voted no.

Earthjustice, for the Alliance for Affordable Energy and Union of Concerned Scientists, asked the LPSC to investigate Meta's Blue Owl / Beignet Investors financing deal and open a prudence review of Entergy's gas plants, so households are not left paying if Meta leaves early.
Outcome: the LPSC declined on 2026-02-25 to investigate Meta's ownership transfer, rejecting the Earthjustice request.
Same groups filed testimony in docket U-37882 (7 new gas plants) asking regulators to slow down, citing secrecy and ratepayer risk if Meta leaves before the contract ends.

Subpoena fight in docket U-37882: the ALJ granted the groups' subpoena for Meta's job, investment and power-need data, but on 2026-08-12 the LPSC voted 3-1 (Lewis against, Campbell absent) to quash it. Speakers from Take Back the Power and LSU's Student Alliance for AI Reform objected at the meeting.

Side dispute settled: after the ALJ sided with the Alliance and UCS on 2026-08-06 over access to 'Attorneys' Eyes Only' material, Entergy and the groups settled on 2026-09-04, giving seven group representatives limited access. It does not give them the Meta records.

Court appeal: the Alliance for Affordable Energy and Union of Concerned Scientists, represented by Earthjustice, asked the 19th Judicial District Court to reverse the LPSC's 'arbitrary and capricious' decision and reinstate the subpoena to Meta. Status: pending; no schedule set as of mid-October 2026.

Hearing in docket U-37882 (7 gas plants for the expansion) opened 2026-10-07 before Chief ALJ Melanie Verzwyvelt; the Alliance for Affordable Energy, Sierra Club and Union of Concerned Scientists challenged costs and the risk that Meta leaves before its 20-year contract ends. Entergy has a settlement with PSC staff. Status: ALJ report pending; LPSC vote set for 2026-12-16.

Landowners along Entergy's planned St. Landry-to-Richland transmission line for Meta (about 450 tracts) and interest groups object that a public-need finding could be used to expropriate right-of-way. LPSC vote on the line set for 2026-12-16.

home_value_acs_median.note: ACS 5-year table B25077, owner-occupied median home value. Each key is the last year of a 5-year window (2024 = 2020-2024), so points move slowly. All points cover years before the announcement; no after point exists yet (2021-2025 window due about December 2026).

rent_fmr_2br.note: HUD Fair Market Rent, 2 bedrooms. Keys are federal fiscal years (FY2027 runs 2026-10-01 to 2027-09-30). Iberville Parish is in the Iberville Parish, LA HUD Metro FMR Area FMR area, so this is the metro-wide number, not a parish-only one.

home_value_zillow_zhvi.note: Zillow Home Value Index, all homes, middle tier, smoothed and seasonally adjusted by Zillow. December value of each year plus the latest month (August 2026), copied unrounded.

rent_zillow_zori.note: Zillow Observed Rent Index, smoothed. December value of each year plus August 2026, unrounded. Zillow publishes no series for Jefferson Davis Parish, so null. Earlier months are blank in the Zillow file, so null.

wage_weekly_qcew.note: Annual average weekly wage. BLS QCEW, all ownerships (own_code 0), all industries (industry_code 10).

jobs_qcew.note: Annual average employment. BLS QCEW, all ownerships (own_code 0), all industries (industry_code 10).

wage_weekly_qcew_q1.note: First quarter only, same quarter each year, kept apart from the annual series. 2026-Q1 is the newest quarter BLS has published (Q2 2026 not out on 2026-10-15) and is preliminary. BLS QCEW, all ownerships (own_code 0), all industries (industry_code 10).

jobs_qcew_q1.note: Employment in March (third month) of each first quarter. 2026-Q1 is preliminary. BLS QCEW, all ownerships (own_code 0), all industries (industry_code 10).

home_power_price_res.note: Tracks Entergy Louisiana only because it serves part of both parishes; the site's own company is not confirmed. Average home power price. Our math: EIA-861 residential revenue divided by residential sales (Sales_Ult_Cust, Part A, Louisiana), so kind is estimate. Calendar years; 2025 is EIA final data released 2026-10-07. One rate per company statewide, so this follows rate changes, not parish differences. Data center rate cases for this company: LPSC dockets U-37425 (Hyperion phase 1 generation, approved 2025-08-20), U-37882 (Meta expansion) and U-37801 (Cottonwood plant purchase); see data/states/LA.json dockets and rate_cases.

sales_tax_collections.note: Not found. Louisiana has no statewide report of local sales tax collections by parish; each parish collector (often the school board) reports on its own. Next place to look: each collector's yearly audit on the Louisiana Legislative Auditor site (https://www.lla.la.gov/). Left null.

before_after.note: Start year 2024 = announcement (Sept 2026) minus 2. Shows change over time side by side. It does not show what caused any change.
